name: Methotrexate
route_note: oral or SC once weekly for autoimmune disease; IV (including high-dose with leucovorin rescue) and intrathecal for cancer

discovery.by: Lederle Laboratories, with Sidney Farber's clinical work on aminopterin
discovery.note: Folate analogues were synthesised at Lederle; aminopterin produced the first remissions in childhood leukaemia (1948), and the methyl derivative amethopterin replaced it.

tagline: Founding antifolate of cancer chemotherapy and anchor drug for rheumatoid arthritis
summary: Methotrexate is a folic acid analogue that blocks dihydrofolate reductase, starving cells of the folate cofactors needed to make DNA. At high doses it treats leukaemias, lymphomas, osteosarcoma and choriocarcinoma; at low weekly doses it is the first-line disease-modifying drug for rheumatoid arthritis and is used in psoriasis and other immune diseases.
mechanism: Methotrexate enters cells via the reduced folate carrier and is polyglutamated, which retains it intracellularly. It binds dihydrofolate reductase about 1,000-fold more tightly than folate, depleting tetrahydrofolate needed for thymidylate and purine synthesis and halting DNA synthesis in S phase.
Leucovorin (folinic acid) bypasses the block and is used to 'rescue' normal cells after high-dose therapy.
In low-dose autoimmune use, inhibition of AICAR transformylase leads to adenosine accumulation, which has anti-inflammatory effects; this is thought to contribute more than antiproliferative action.
uses: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (including CNS prophylaxis, intrathecal)
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma and primary CNS lymphoma (high dose)
Breast, head and neck and bladder cancer regimens
Rheumatoid arthritis, polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis
Off-label: ectopic pregnancy, Crohn disease, vasculitis, GVHD prophylaxis

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Lederle chemists synthesise amethopterin (methotrexate) as part of a folate antagonist programme.

history.title: Leukaemia remissions
history.detail: Sidney Farber reports temporary remissions in children with acute leukaemia treated with aminopterin.

history.title: Choriocarcinoma cure
history.detail: Min Chiu Li and Roy Hertz report the first cures of a metastatic solid tumour (choriocarcinoma) with methotrexate.

history.title: Psoriasis
history.detail: FDA approves methotrexate for severe psoriasis.

history.title: Rheumatoid arthritis
history.detail: FDA approves methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis.

history.title: Weekly-dosing safety
history.detail: Repeated fatal daily-instead-of-weekly dosing errors lead to labelling and packaging changes in many countries.

history.title: EMA review
history.detail: EMA recommends new measures (packaging, alert cards) to prevent daily-dosing errors.

pk.half_life: about 3–10 hours at low dose; 8–15 hours at high dose
pk.bioavailability: oral about 60% at low doses, falling at higher doses
pk.metabolism: intracellular polyglutamation; partial hepatic hydroxylation to 7-OH-MTX

serious: acute kidney injury with high dose
safety.boxed_warning: Boxed warning for serious toxic reactions including death, embryo-fetal toxicity and contraindication in pregnancy for non-cancer use; must be given once weekly for non-oncologic indications.

facts: Low-dose regimens for arthritis are taken once a week; daily intake by mistake has caused fatal toxicity.
Glucarpidase, an enzyme that cleaves methotrexate, is used for toxic plasma levels in patients with renal impairment.
